definition: A learner who studied a language before and kept almost none of it.
business_context_example: Every false beginner opens the same way: I understand everything, I just can't speak.
translation_bg: фалшив начинаещ, учил е и е забравил

definition: Out of practice, so what you knew comes back slowly.
business_context_example: My English is rusty means I haven't used it since a holiday in 2019.

definition: The language you grew up speaking.
business_context_example: Your mother tongue helps you more than you think and betrays you in the word order.

definition: From the very beginning, with nothing behind you.
business_context_example: Starting from scratch at forty is easier than at fourteen. You know why you're there.

definition: To improve something you once knew.
business_context_example: I'll brush up on my English before the trip, said every traveller, three days before the trip.

definition: To know just enough of a language to manage.
business_context_example: I get by in English means airports yes, contracts no.

definition: How advanced you are, usually named A2, B1, B2 or C1.
business_context_example: Everybody guesses their language level one step above the test and one below their mother.

definition: Practising a real situation by acting it out in the lesson.
business_context_example: Nobody wants the role play. Everybody remembers the role play a month later.

definition: Work given to do between lessons.
business_context_example: Adults do their homework on the bus, eleven minutes before the lesson, and call it revision.

definition: To tell somebody their English was wrong and give the right form.
business_context_example: Correct me every time, they say in week one. Correct me sometimes, they mean by week three.

definition: The person you actually speak with, in or out of class.
business_context_example: A practice partner who is slightly worse than you is worth more than a perfect one.

definition: To write down what you want to remember from a lesson.
business_context_example: Taking notes feels like learning. Reading them on Thursday is where the learning happens.

definition: To go back over something you have already studied.
business_context_example: Revise the phrases from two weeks ago, not the ones from yesterday. Yesterday is still warm.

definition: To say politely that you didn't follow something.
business_context_example: Asking for clarification in a lesson costs nothing. Not asking costs the rest of the hour.

phrase: on the tip of my tongue
definition: Almost remembered, and refusing to arrive.
business_context_example: It was on the tip of my tongue for the whole meeting and arrived in the lift afterwards.
audio_text: on the tip of my tongue

definition: To remember nothing at all at the moment you need it.
business_context_example: I drew a blank on a word I had used twice that morning.

definition: A word that looks familiar and means something else entirely.
business_context_example: The false friend gets you once, publicly, and then never again.

definition: To sound vaguely familiar without being quite remembered.
business_context_example: That word rings a bell, which in practice means I will look it up again tonight.

definition: A card with a word on one side and its meaning on the other.
business_context_example: Forty flashcards made on Sunday, four reviewed on Monday, zero on Tuesday.

definition: To learn something so it can be recalled exactly.
business_context_example: You can memorise a hundred words and still be silent, which is the whole problem.

definition: To check a word in a dictionary or online.
business_context_example: The word you look up twice is the word you should have written down the first time.
translation_bg: да си я проверя в речника

definition: Unable to speak because you are nervous.
business_context_example: He was tongue-tied for a year, then perfectly fine the day his boss left the room.

definition: To speak quietly and unclearly, usually out of doubt.
business_context_example: People mumble the words they aren't sure of, which is exactly the moment to say them louder.

definition: To trip on a word while saying it.
business_context_example: She stumbled over one word and apologised for the whole sentence.

definition: To keep a real exchange going, not just answer questions.
business_context_example: Holding a conversation for ten minutes is a bigger milestone than any exam.

definition: To forget what you were saying halfway through saying it.
business_context_example: I lost my train of thought in English and found it again in Bulgarian, which helped nobody.

definition: To answer well without time to prepare.
business_context_example: Thinking on your feet in a second language is a skill, and it arrives last.

definition: To pause before speaking because you aren't sure.
business_context_example: Everybody hesitates. Native speakers just hesitate in a way nobody notices.

definition: Able to speak without stopping to build every sentence.
business_context_example: Fluent gets used as a compliment and defined as whatever the speaker can't do yet.

definition: To understand the general meaning without every word.
business_context_example: Getting the gist is enough for 90% of a meeting and nobody admits it.

definition: To hear and understand somebody's words.
business_context_example: I didn't catch that is the most useful sentence nobody wants to say.

definition: To ask somebody to reduce their speed.
business_context_example: Ask them to speak slowly and they will, for about two sentences.

definition: Sound around a conversation that makes listening harder.
business_context_example: Your English gets noticeably worse in a café, and that isn't your English.

definition: The written words shown on screen while people speak.
business_context_example: English subtitles on English audio is the single cheapest lesson available.

definition: To speak while somebody else is still speaking.
business_context_example: On a call in a second language, being talked over feels personal. It usually isn't.
translation_bg: да говоря в устата на някого

definition: The way somebody's speech sounds, shaped by where they come from.
business_context_example: Two speakers, one accent each, and the meeting works fine. That is the normal case.

definition: Surrounding yourself with the language so you meet it all day.
business_context_example: Immersion sounds like moving abroad. It also means changing your phone's language.

definition: Two people teaching each other their languages.
business_context_example: A language exchange works until one of you is more polite than the other.

definition: To continue doing something you have started.
business_context_example: Keep it up is easy to say in October and worth saying again in February.

definition: To slip below the pace of the course or the group.
business_context_example: You fall behind quietly, over three weeks, and notice it in one lesson.

definition: To slow down after a good period, without deciding to.
business_context_example: Nobody decides to quit. They lose momentum in a busy week and never restart.

definition: To do the unglamorous amount of work the thing requires.
business_context_example: Talent decides month one. Putting in the hours decides everything after that.

definition: To carry on despite it being difficult or dull.
business_context_example: The people who stick with it are rarely the ones who were best in September.

definition: A period where you work as usual and stop feeling better.
business_context_example: The plateau is where most people quit, about four weeks before it ends.

definition: The moment something difficult suddenly works.
business_context_example: The breakthrough arrives on an ordinary Tuesday, in a sentence you didn't plan.

definition: To form thoughts directly, without translating first.
business_context_example: You start thinking in English with three words, not three paragraphs.

definition: The milestone nobody plans and everybody reports.
business_context_example: She dreamt in English for the first time and told four people before lunch.

definition: To learn a language gradually, without formal study.
business_context_example: Children pick up a language. Adults learn one, and then pretend they picked it up.
translation_bg: да усвоя език по естествен път

definition: So familiar that it takes no thought at all.
business_context_example: The phrase you fought with in March is second nature by November, unnoticed.

phrase: come on in leaps and bounds
definition: To improve very quickly over a short period.
business_context_example: Her listening came on in leaps and bounds the month she stopped using subtitles.
audio_text: come on in leaps and bounds
